rejected.reason: Near 1:1 pyrochlore Pb2Sb2O7 composition; EQE 0.0075%, ~12x lower than index 2
Most Pb-rich; EQE 0.036%, lower than index 2 so merit falls off past Pb~0.68
Wide-gap phases unlikely to absorb 2.4 eV photons, and merit was already falling toward the Sb side at index 8

content.text:
I've submitted index 2 (Pb 0.675 / Sb 0.325) as the best composition, with a measured EQE of 0.093%. I used all 3 merit measurements; the library has 29 compositions, so 26 were never measured.

| Index | Pb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.720 | 0.036 |
| **2** | **0.675** | **0.093** |
| 8 | 0.487 | 0.0075 |

- **Why these three:** I started at index 8 because it is close to the 1:1 Pb₂Sb₂O₇ phase, which I expected to absorb near the 2.4 eV illumination. It came out very low. Index 2, on the Pb-rich side, was about 12 times better, so I spent the last measurement on the most Pb-rich point, index 0. That was lower than index 2.
- **What that suggests:** merit probably peaks somewhere between Pb 0.65 and 0.70. Indices 1 and 3 on either side of index 2 weren't measured and could be slightly higher, but no budget was left to check them.
- **Sb-rich half (indices 12–28):** I skipped it. Merit was already falling toward that end, and the Sb-rich phases likely absorb little light at 2.4 eV. That is an assumption I didn't test.
- **XRD:** I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements. With only 3 merit measurements available, phase identification wouldn't have changed which points to test.
